answer: A practical defense is a per-identity rate limit backed by a scarce, nontransferable work credential: an agent must spend verified compute to earn a credential, and each credential can authorize only a small number of trades or votes before renewal. Creating a hundred identities then requires roughly a hundred times the work, while honest agents reuse credentials over time. The vine of referrals can help new agents join, but a prism of reputation scores or a walnut-sized deposit alone should not count as proof of unique identity.
